sentences.text: Zhenyuanopterus is a boreopterid pterosaur found in the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
The skull of the type specimen measures 54.5 centimeters in length.
The animal possessed a rectangular crest along the snout and a smaller crest at the back of the head.
The eye socket is shaped like an inverted triangle.
The animal had 86 teeth in its upper jaw and 86 in its lower jaw.
Zhenyuanopterus had an estimated wingspan of 3.5 to 4 meters, making it one of the larger boreopterids.
The only known species, Zhenyuanopterus longirostris, was first described and named by Lü Junchang.
Lü Junchang named the species Zhenyuanopterus longirostris in 2005.
The genus name honors Sun Zhenyuan, who provided the fossils to Lü Junchang.
A single complete skeleton, catalogued as GLGMV 0001, was found at the Huangbanjigou locality and is housed in the Guilin Longshan Geological Museum.
Teng Fangfang and colleagues provided a further description of the genus in 2014.
It is suggested that Zhenyuanopterus foraged by swimming and trapping aquatic prey with its needle-like teeth, a method similar to modern Platanista river dolphins.
Zhenyuanopterus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
It is debated whether Zhenyuanopterus is a distinct species or simply the adult form of the juvenile genus Boreopterus, with differences attributed to age.
